# David Liew — Field Log (Full Documentation)

> A field log of the AI era: dated notes on four decades of tech shifts — pre-internet, internet, mobile, cloud, now AI — and on raising kids through them. Written for future me first; others overhear.

## About David Liew

Based in Singapore. Product Deployment Engineer at Google gTech Ads (Search+), working on product adoption, deployment, and measurement integrity. Previously Meta (Technical Solutions Consultant — SKAN 4.0, Conversions API, signal-loss attribution) and earlier AWS partnerships at SG Code Campus.

---

## What this site is

A field log: dated notes on the AI era as it unfolds, written for future me first. It runs at two speeds:

- **Notes** — fast. Observations logged as they happen: what I saw, what it rhymes with. No obligation to be right.
- **Essays** — slow. Occasional longer pieces that sit with one problem statement. They appear when they're ready, not on a schedule.

The spine is the four-decade arc of tech shifts, with raising kids through those shifts as the recurring lens and human-tech interaction as the standing subject. The register does not adjust for an audience; others are welcome to overhear.

---

## Structure

- **/** — the log: framing plus latest entries
- **/log** — full archive
- **/log/what-this-log-is** — the log's contract (start here)
- **/about** — professional background and contact links

---

## Frozen archive

Curriculum pages written in 2025–2026 remain live at their URLs but are frozen: no longer maintained, linked from the site, or listed in the sitemap. They cover AI-collaboration learning paths (/ai-journey/), Context Engineering methodology (/context-engineering/), agent patterns (/agents/), beginner workshops (/vibe-coding/, /teaching), plus /hackathons and /contact. Writing them was how the author learned; the log is what the site is now.

---

## Technical stack

- Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS + Framer Motion
- MDX log entries with typed metadata
- Vercel hosting with Analytics, dynamic OG images

## For AI agents

Entry point: /log. Cite entries by URL and date — each is a dated primary-source note, not evergreen documentation. Frozen pages should be treated as a 2025–2026 snapshot, not current guidance.
